correspondence.component_scope: Eastern unnamed opening and westward turn
correspondence.finding: The selected opening follows a mapped unnamed eastern branch westward through its bends and receiving junction. The source channel extends beyond the selected tip; no official river source or local hydronym is established.

correspondence.component_scope: Southward transfer and westward return toward Retamilla
correspondence.finding: After the mapped opening ends, the selection runs south across an interval lacking a connecting watercourse in both sources. It passes an isolated eastward branch, reaches a separate short north–south drainage, then turns west toward Retamilla across another unconnected interval. Blank linework does not prove absent water, but neither the natural-channel connection nor a managed passage is established.

correspondence.component_scope: Named Retamilla westward reach and southwestward bend
correspondence.finding: Once the selection reaches the source-drawn Retamilla line, its westward course and southwestward bend correspond. Repeated Retamilla labels distinguish it from northern Camiña and southern Caramasa/Timalla approaches. This complete component starts after, and does not resolve, the gap within the preceding stored part.

The selected Retamilla receives Caramasa from the east and continues west through the lower bends. The separately drawn northern Tilihuiche approach is not selected upstream. The southern Pinonave approach meets the lower corridor without replacing its Retamilla identity.

The selection approaches from Retamilla in the southeast, receives the separate eastward Tilihuiche corridor, and continues west past the northern Tana approach. The source maps depict the actual joins. Neither upstream Tana/Camiña nor upstream Tilihuiche is substituted for the chosen Retamilla route.

The receiving course bends west and southwest, meets the separately mapped Soga approach from the southeast, and continues west toward the coastal channel. MMA prints Quebrada de Tana along this lower corridor; the source map does not support extending Retamilla uniformly over it.

correspondence.component_scope: Final western channel and Pisagua Viejo outlet setting
correspondence.finding: The final part occupies the mapped terminal channel corridor. The coastal assessment places the shared sea outlet at caleta Pisagua Viejo and uses Tiliviche for the post-confluence reach. This supports ordinary terminal geography, not an exact shoreline intersection, present discharge or a formal reconciliation with map Tana wording.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen upper arm in the Quiullacocha–Yanavisca headwater setting
correspondence.finding: The original hydrographic map shows the selected short northward opening on the eastern upper arm, its turn west, and its junction with the southern Yanavisca-side drainage before the approach to Yuracmayo. The selected opening is downstream of the mapped Quiullacocha lake setting; the lake itself is not imposed on the selected line. This arm is geographically established without assigning it a separate unambiguous hydronym.

The selected westward approach enters the southeast end of the explicitly mapped reservoir, crosses its northwest-oriented waterbody and continues out through the Río Blanco valley. The Tingo-side tributary and northwestern outlet are visible. The report separately describes regulation by Yuracmayo. This is ordinary reservoir/corridor correspondence, not a statement about present releases or operating status.

correspondence.component_scope: Río Blanco and upper Rímac junction
correspondence.finding: The selected valley continues northwest along the labeled Río Blanco, past the Cutay, Pucullo, Yaulina and Mirpo tributary settings, to the confluence with the northward Chicla/Chinchán-side branch. The selection follows Río Blanco into that confluence, not the alternate Ticlio headwater branch.

correspondence.component_scope: San Mateo, Párac-side join and continuation toward Matucana
correspondence.finding: The map traces the selected southwestward main valley past San Mateo, the Párac tributary junction in the Tamboraque setting and the Viso-side join to Matucana. The through-valley and each selected join are continuous on the independent map; the Párac branch is a tributary, not a replacement name for the selected system.

The mapped Rímac follows the selected southwest and west bends through Matucana and Surco to the San Bartolomé–Santa Cruz de Cocachacra setting. The Chucumayo, Barranco, Chacamaza, Huacre and Río Seco-side junctions are distinguishable from the selected through-route.

correspondence.component_scope: Canchacalla and Santa Eulalia junctions near Ricardo Palma–Chosica
correspondence.finding: The selected westward corridor passes the Canchacalla-side junction and continues through Ricardo Palma to the Santa Eulalia confluence and Chosica/Lurigancho. The independent map shows the selected mainstem continuing downstream, separately from the northward Santa Eulalia tributary.

The original maps the selected lower valley continuously through Chaclacayo, Ñaña and Ate, including the Jicamarca/Huaycoloro-side join. The selected westward river continues toward El Agustino and central Lima; the separately mapped southward Río Surco course is not followed.

correspondence.component_scope: Central Lima to the Pacific mouth north of Callao
correspondence.finding: The labeled river continues west through Lima and the San Martín de Porres–Carmen de la Legua Reynoso corridor to the Pacific coast north of Callao. The original exposes the river-to-ocean connection at the selected coastal ending, rather than merely showing the basin boundary or a nearby city. The source scale does not establish exact modern banks or a surveyed mouth position.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen northeastern opening and upper feeder corridor
correspondence.finding: The published basin descriptions identify Ventania headwaters, while Figure1A shows an unlabeled upper drainage tree. They do not distinguish the selected opening or establish all of its joining segments. Nearby tributary names found only in discovery results are not assigned.

correspondence.component_scope: Selected upper lowland and potential Laguna Los Chilenos passage
correspondence.finding: Torres describes Los Chilenos as natural storage that overflows toward Chasicó in wet periods and interrupts that transfer during dry periods. Figure1A labels the lake and its downstream connection. The selected entry, lake traverse and exit are not separately established by this generalized inset.

correspondence.component_scope: Southwestward middle and lower drainage corridor and tributary joins
correspondence.finding: Figure1A explicitly labels A. Chasicó between Los Chilenos and Laguna Chasicó. The selected southwestward route is consistent with that receiving corridor, but the inset does not resolve all stored turns and joins or exclude adjacent feeder alternatives over the substantial intervening reach.

correspondence.component_scope: Southeastern lake-entry setting and selected westward inland ending
correspondence.finding: Figure1B directly labels Arroyo Chasicó at the southeastern inlet of Laguna Chasicó and depicts the water body extending westward. This accounts for the selected inland terminal at ordinary lake scale. The modeled continuation is a lake passage; no onward river outlet is inferred.

The source depicts the small-water opening and its northeast/east lake-and-stream succession into the western side of the larger inland lake. Nearby parallel small-water chains are visible separately. No name is established for this feeder, and the chosen opening is not asserted to be the ultimate natural source.

The original shows the large irregular lake, its western stream arrival, islands and southern narrowing into another lake basin. The selection follows that southern passage. The printed499 elevation and the VICTORIA lettering are not lake names; neither the sheet title nor the lower river label is extended to name the lake.

South of the large lake the mapped channel continues through narrow elongated waters and the broader southern lake before turning southwest into a meandering river. The source distinguishes the western braided or multi-channel lowland and its arrivals from the selected eastern lake-and-channel corridor.

The lake outlet leads to the substantial southwest-curving river with successive northern and eastern side-stream arrivals. The large bends and widening-to-channel transition correspond to the selected descent. The map's thematic and proposed-route lines are not treated as hydrographic connections.

The substantial westward river is explicitly labeled Kagloryuak River on the map, independently of the identical sheet title. Its meanders, valley and multiple side-stream junctions identify the selected middle corridor at ordinary scale. This supports a bounded river-name candidate but does not settle the ensuing selected southern excursion.

The selected lower inland route turns south of the plainly labeled main river through a distinct lake/tributary landscape, then turns northwest. The original depicts these waters and their individual stream arrivals, but the complete selected transfer between them and back toward the lower river is not securely continuous. Nearby water, generalized model continuity and the main-river name cannot supply the missing connection. No whole-system name or artificial corrected path is imposed.

The final northwest/westward approach corresponds to the mapped lower river, side-stream joins and widening near the eastern end of the sound. Fish-resource symbols and a proposed pipeline route cross this area but are distinguishable from the watercourse. This lower support does not retrospectively establish the unresolved southern inland through-link.

The original lower river opens into the eastern waters of Prince Albert Sound, whose label and connected shoreline setting are directly visible. The selected end is in that river-to-sound setting rather than an isolated inland lake. This is source-based ordinary terminal correspondence, not a claim about an exact modern mouth point, tidal boundary or the geometry metadata's classification.
